# Implementation Readiness Checklist: Markdown Syntax and Formatting Options

**Purpose**: Validate the quality, clarity, completeness, and consistency of the requirements before implementation begins
**Created**: 2026-08-15
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) | [plan.md](../plan.md) | [contract](../contracts/markdown-syntax.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command. It tests the *requirements* (spec/plan/contract), not the implementation.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are functional requirements defined for each of the six configurable options (hard breaks, strikethrough, tables, task lists, math, autolink)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003–FR-008]
- [ ] CHK002 Is a requirement specified for restoring saved markdown settings on startup (FR-012), and separately for fresh-install/missing-config defaults (FR-013)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012/FR-013]
- [ ] CHK003 Is raw source-view immunity specified — that source view always renders verbatim characters regardless of toggle state? [Completeness, Spec §Edge Cases / Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK004 Is a save round-trip requirement defined asserting that documents containing disabled syntax save byte-for-byte with no escaping, altering, or dropping of characters? [Completeness, Spec §Edge Cases / SC-004]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the typing path covered — a requirement that typing a disabled syntax's delimiters (e.g., `~~`) must not trigger auto-formatting, not just loading already-written text? [Gap, Spec §US1 S3/S4]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the treatment of GFM footnote syntax (a construct outside the six options) documented as always-on, so its behaviour is not left implicit? [Gap, Assumption]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK007 Are the six toggle labels specified exactly as shown to the user, with no ambiguity about wording? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003–FR-008]
- [ ] CHK008 Does the hard-break requirement clearly distinguish a hard break within a paragraph from a new paragraph — i.e., paragraph structure must remain unchanged? [Clarity, Spec §US2 S1/S2]
- [ ] CHK009 Is "literal plaintext" for a disabled syntax unambiguous — delimiters rendered verbatim, neither escaped nor removed? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the scope of "automatic link detection for URLs and emails" defined (which URL/email patterns auto-link)? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK011 Are the math delimiters specified precisely (inline `$…$` vs block `$$…$$`), matching the toggle label? [Clarity, Spec §US1 S5 / FR-007]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the "300 milliseconds" (SC-002) and "10 seconds" (SC-005) bound given a measurement method, or is "immediately" (FR-010) asserted without a verification path? [Ambiguity, Spec §SC-002/SC-005]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK013 Do the FR-013 defaults align across the requirements, Key Entities, and acceptance scenarios (all five syntaxes on, hard breaks off)? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013 / Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK014 Is the Markdown area's immediate-apply model consistent with the dialog's per-area persistence rules — e.g., distinguished from the Theme editor setting that is Save-gated? [Consistency]
- [ ] CHK015 Are the edge-case statements (source-view immunity, no document content mutation) consistent with FR-014/FR-015? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK016 Do the US1/US2 acceptance scenarios map one-to-one to FR-003–FR-008 without omissions or contradictions? [Consistency, Traceability, Spec §US1/US2]
- [ ] CHK017 Does US3 S3's claim that cursor/scroll are "maintained" conflict with the plan's best-effort character-offset restoration caveat (R6) — is the requirement over-promising? [Conflict, Spec §US3 / Plan R6]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK018 Is SC-001 objectively measurable (100% of the 6 options togglable independently, with a definition of "independently")? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK019 Is SC-004's round-trip criterion defined with a concrete assertion (exact bytes on disk, both disable→save and enable→save directions)? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK020 Is SC-005 (usability, under 10 s) given an evaluation methodology and participant criteria, or is it unverifiable? [Gap, Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK021 Is "preserved undo/redo history" (US3 S2 / FR-011) verifiable given the reconfiguration mechanism, and is a requirement→scenario ID scheme established for traceability? [Traceability, Gap, Spec §US3]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK022 Is the primary flow covered — open settings, reach the Markdown area, toggle a switch, see the open editor re-render? [Coverage, Spec §US1]
- [ ] CHK023 Are multi-tab scenarios covered for dirty state, unsaved edits, undo/redo history, cursor, and scroll — not just rendering? [Coverage, Spec §US3]
- [ ] CHK024 Is the persistence scenario covered for both custom-value restore and fresh-install/missing-config defaults? [Coverage, Spec §US4]
- [ ] CHK025 Is the exception scenario of a corrupt or unreadable settings file covered with a safe-defaults requirement? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK026 Is the scenario of a syntax toggle occurring while a save is in flight covered (revision/dirty-state guard)? [Gap, Exception Flow]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK027 Are unclosed or partial delimiters (`~`, `$`) specified for both enabled and disabled states, without layout breakage? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK028 Is rapid toggle switching specified to settle on the final state without stutter or a stuck intermediate state? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK029 Are mixed-option combinations defined — e.g., tables off while task lists on, or hard breaks on inside table cells? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK030 Is the toggling state with no open tab, a single tab, or only a source-view tab specified? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK031 Are disabled-syntax delimiters inside code spans or fenced code blocks specified to stay literal regardless of toggle state? [Gap]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK032 Is the 300 ms all-tab re-render bound (SC-002) recorded as an NFR with a stated, non-flaky verification method (manual vs automated)? [NFR, Gap, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK033 Are accessibility requirements specified for the six new settings toggles — keyboard operability and labelled controls consistent with existing switches? [NFR, Gap]
- [ ] CHK034 Is there an explicit requirement that reconfiguration performs no work on the typing/keystroke path (typing latency unaffected)? [NFR, Gap]
- [ ] CHK035 Is undo/redo integrity across reconfiguration an explicit requirement — not merely "not cleared" but validated step-maps — given schema-constancy is the mechanism? [NFR, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK036 Is a bound on concurrently live editor instances for the reconfiguration fan-out stated (scale/performance envelope)? [NFR, Gap]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK037 Are the five recorded Assumptions (apply model, default rationale, source-view immunity, no content mutation, scope) explicit and traceable to requirement wording? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK038 Is the dependency on the existing settings IPC surface — no new channel, reuse of `settings:get`/`settings:update` — documented in the requirements? [Dependency, Contract]
- [ ] CHK039 Is the assumption that runtime reconfiguration preserves undo history validated by evidence (research R1/R3) rather than asserted? [Assumption, Plan R3]
- [ ] CHK040 Is the cursor/scroll restoration explicitly framed as best-effort in the requirements, not over-promised, and are the direct-dependency promotions (micromark/mdast GFM packages) documented? [Conflict, Dependency, Plan R6]

## Notes

- Items marked [Gap] flag requirements currently absent from the spec; decide whether to add them to `spec.md` (recorded decision) or accept as out of scope before implementing.
- Constitution relevance: Principle III (data loss — FR-011, SC-004) and Principle V (round-trip, settings validation tests) gate this feature; Principle II is not touched (no new path handling).
